slides.title: Clothing, Fashion, and Sustainability
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 7 English, Unit 3: Clothing, Fashion, and Sustainability. This unit explores the world of clothing, fashion, and sustainability.You will learn how clothes are made, why the choices we make as consumers matter, and what young people around the world are doing to protect the environment through sustainable fashion.You will build your skills with multi-word verbs such as put on, dress up and throw away, and you will learn how the passive voice and modal verbs describe processes, rules and recommendations.Alongside the topic work, you will read the story A Voice in the Valley, about a quiet girl named Sana in highland Ethiopia who discovers that her writing can inspire an entire community. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use vocabulary related to clothing, materials, fast fashion, and the environment.
Understand and use multi-word verbs (phrasal verbs) such as put on, take off, dress up, throw away, and give away.
Form sentences in the present passive ("Cotton is grown in many countries") and past passive ("The dress was made by hand").
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use vocabulary related to clothing, materials, fast fashion, and the environment. You will also understand and use multi-word verbs (phrasal verbs) such as put on, take off, dress up, throw away, and give away. You will also form sentences in the present passive ("Cotton is grown in many countries") and past passive ("The dress was made by hand"). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: alliteration, rhyme, rhythm, repetition, punctuation, figurative. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The True Cost of Fast Fashion
From Curtains to Catwalk: An Interview with Amara
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The True Cost of Fast Fashion and From Curtains to Catwalk: An Interview with Amara. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Multi-Word Verbs
bullets: Multi-word verbs, often called phrasal verbs, join a main verb to a particle such as on, off, up or away, and together they create a meaning the verb...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Multi-Word Verbs. Multi-word verbs, often called phrasal verbs, join a main verb to a particle such as on, off, up or away, and together they create a meaning the verb alone does not carry, so put on means to wear while put off means to delay. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1: Describe Your Outfit with Multi-Word Verbs
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Describe Your Outfit with Multi-Word Verbs. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
